financing.summary: Brookfield Residential is a land developer first: at 30 Sep 2026 it controlled 58,931 lots on a Brookfield-share basis (127,242 managed lots), and it pays for land with Brookfield Corporation equity, four unsecured 144A note series ($1.63B), a $675M unsecured revolver (drawn $586M, only $15M free at Q3 2026) and project loans. It is moving its land book off balance sheet by selling stakes to capital partners: 80% of five master-planned communities in Jan 2025 (NASH invested in five MPCs, announced Mar 2025), the Kolter Land partnership in the Southeast, and the Trez Capital JV. It now puts 5-50% equity into new land deals and also manages land with no equity. Its own land-banking counterparty is affiliate Brookfield Wealth Solutions (lot financing arrangements plus a 2025 land option agreement), and it invests in landbanking vehicles (Homebuilder Finance) and markets land banking to other builders. That makes it more a competitor or co-investor for Domain than a borrower. The opening for a third-party land banker is small but real: the $600M 6.25% notes mature in Sep 2027, Moody's moved the outlook to negative in Oct 2026, and the revolver is almost fully drawn.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed, moving to land-light. The company describes an asset-light managed-land model: it sources a capital partner for each new land deal and invests 5-50% equity, keeps its existing wholly owned land, and may manage land with no equity. Growth is to come mainly from JVs and managed-only assets, which earn development management fees and secure finished lots for its own homebuilding. Target leverage is 40-50%, matched to active land and housing inventory.

lots.source_title: Brookfield Residential Q3 2026 Interim Report (MD&A and notes, approved 2026-10-28)
lots.note: Brookfield Residential share. Owned = 35,611 lots owned directly (Canada 23,423; U.S. 12,188) + 11,907 lots held through 47 unconsolidated entities. Optioned = 11,413 lots of 'inventory not owned' (consolidated land under financing arrangements and lots under option), of which 11,253 are in Northern California, 57 in Southern California and 103 in Texas. pct_optioned computed here (11,413 / 58,931). Managed lots at 100% (incl. JV partners' and managed-only interests): 127,242. Dec 31 2025: 58,155 controlled (34,213 owned, 12,432 JV, 11,510 not owned). Years supply not disclosed. Note that inventory-not-owned book value is only $19.3M, so most of these lots appear to be optioned or financed rather than balance-sheet land.

land_banking.description: BWS is a Brookfield Corporation affiliate. It holds land under financing arrangements that Brookfield Residential buys back as lots, and from 2025 a land option agreement under which Brookfield Residential pays option maintenance fees and deposits for the right to buy lots. At 30 Sep 2026 the related liability was $17.2M, inventory not owned was $19.3M, deposits were $12.7M on the financing arrangements and $24.5M on the option agreements, and capitalized option fees were $6.5M. In the first nine months of 2026 it paid $49.2M for lots and $16.1M for land bought from BWS.
land_banking.source_title: Brookfield Residential Q3 2026 Interim Report (MD&A and notes, approved 2026-10-28)
land_banking.note: In the 2025 Annual Report, 2025 lot takedowns from BWS were $83.1M (2024: $60.3M) and the liability fell from $117.3M (Dec 2024) to $53.7M (Dec 2025); the land option agreement with BWS was entered in 2025. amount_usd_m is the outstanding liability at Q3 2026, not the program size, which is not disclosed. Lot count not disclosed.

land_banking.counterparty: Homebuilder Finance (Brookfield Residential US Land Holdings LLC, II LLC and III)
land_banking.description: Brookfield-affiliated landbanking vehicles that Brookfield Residential invests in, so here it is on the land-banker side. It holds 49.0%, 22.2% and 26.5% interests, carried at fair value as 'Homebuilder Finance Investments' ($63.6M at 30 Sep 2026; $78.0M at Dec 2025). It also lends to Homebuilder Finance: up to $50M at SOFR+2.0-2.75%, with $9.0M outstanding at Dec 2025 (Dec 2024: $56.8M under a $125M line).
land_banking.source_title: Brookfield Residential Q3 2026 Interim Report (MD&A and notes, approved 2026-10-28)
land_banking.note: Ownership percentages and loan terms come from the 2025 Annual Report, Note 3 and receivables note (https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/097dc95ddd47-brookfieldr25d6-prodb938-e22e/media/project/brp/brp/global/modules/financials-and-disclosures/annual-and-quarterly-reports/2025-annual-report.pdf). At 30 Sep 2026 Brookfield Residential had $62M of mostly non-refundable deposits and entitlement costs and a $283M remaining exercise price, up from $21M and $180M at Dec 2025. A further $114.1M of deposits backs land purchase obligations with $1.3B committed (Dec 2025: $637.4M).

capital_events.description: MPC Recapitalization: sold an 80% interest in five subsidiaries holding the land of five master-planned communities. Total cash consideration was $654.8M after a purchase-price true-up, with a $73.7M gain. The retained 20% is deconsolidated into unconsolidated entities.

Paid $350M of dividends to Brookfield Corporation in 2025 (2024: $475M). Also placed $299.8M on deposit with Brookfield Corporation under a new interest agreement.
capital_events.note: Dated to fiscal year-end; the quarterly dividends included $300M in the first nine months of 2025.

capital_events.description: Entered a land option agreement with affiliate Brookfield Wealth Solutions, paying option maintenance fees for the right to buy lots. Deposits were $15.5M at Dec 2025 and $24.5M at Sep 2026.

North America Sekisui House invested in five Brookfield Residential MPCs (Austin, Phoenix, Denver, Northern California added). The combined partnership holds about $1.6B of US real estate assets and about 30,000 single-family lots under management across 11 states and 13 markets.

joint_ventures.description: Strategic partnership in which Brookfield Residential took an ownership position in Kolter Land. It supplies finished lots and mixed-use pads to builders in Florida, Tennessee, Georgia and the Carolinas and is headed by Jim Harvey, former President of Kolter Land. It closed 11 Nov 2024. Brookfield Residential's 2025 Annual Report says it is adding to its Southeastern managed land through this partnership.
joint_ventures.source_title: Kolter Group release: Brookfield Residential has acquired an ownership position in Kolter Land (2024-11-21)
joint_ventures.note: Stake size not disclosed. Closing date 2024-11-11 per Cleary Gottlieb (https://www.clearygottlieb.com/news-and-insights/news-listing/brookfield-residential-in-strategic-partnership-with-kolter-land). In Oct 2026 HousingWire cited 'Newland and Kolter transactions' as Brookfield examples of investing in land operators before buying them outright; no buyout of Kolter has been announced.

joint_ventures.description: Long-running land partnership, expanded in March 2025 when NASH invested in five Brookfield Residential MPCs. It covers about 30,000 managed lots and about $1.6B of US assets in 13 markets, with Brookfield Residential as development manager.

It earned $36.1M of development management fees from them in the first nine months of 2026 and bought $222.8M of finished lots from them.

competitor_links.relationship: Brookfield Residential's land website markets land banking to homebuilders ('structured, stable capital' for balance-sheet flexibility) alongside lot servicing. Its Q3 2026 profile says US builders increasingly seek off-balance-sheet capital. The MD&A lists 'providing landbanking services' among the land platform's strategies. This makes it a direct competitor to Domain for builder lot-option capital.
competitor_links.note: The site's counters (managed lots, active land banks) render as 0, so it gives no program size.

competitor_links.relationship: Indirect people link only: Andrew Brausa co-founded Domain, later set up and led Brookfield Asset Management's land financing strategies, then left for Apollo in March 2025 to run Olympus Housing Capital. No public Domain-Brookfield Residential transaction was found.
competitor_links.source_title: IPE Real Assets: Brausa to lead Apollo's newly formed US homebuilder finance company (2025-06-30)

ma.source_title: Trez Capital news release: Brookfield Residential and Trez Capital form JV (Osprey Creek) (2025-06-02)

gaps: Revolver administrative agent and lender group: not publicly disclosed (private company; 144A notes, no SEC filings since 2015).
Senior notes trustee and CUSIPs: not disclosed in the reports.
Plan to refinance the $600M 6.25% notes due Sep 2027: management says it is 'evaluating options'; no offering announced as of 2026-11-19.
Buyer of the 80% MPC Recapitalization stake (Jan 2025): not named in the filings; NASH is the probable counterparty but not confirmed.
Kolter Land partnership: ownership percentage and capital committed are not publicly disclosed.
BWS land option agreement: lot count, program size and pricing are not publicly disclosed.

Third-party land-banking partners (Millrose, Kennedy Lewis, TPG Angelo Gordon, Domain, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, etc.): none publicly disclosed. Brookfield Residential's lot option financing appears to be with its affiliate BWS.
Millrose Properties / Kennedy Lewis / TPG Angelo Gordon: no public link to Brookfield Residential found (Millrose names Brookfield Properties among its competitors per the project competitor file).
Builders served by Brookfield's own land-banking offering and by Homebuilder Finance: not publicly disclosed.
Years of lot supply: not disclosed.
No builder acquisition or sale by Brookfield Residential was found for 2025 to Nov 2026 (company press list, sitemap and two web searches checked).

Brookfield Corporation parent-level support: no guarantee of Brookfield Residential's debt is disclosed; the parent funds it through equity, takes dividends ($350M in 2025, $475M in 2024) and holds an interest-bearing deposit agreement.
